og.title: Center for Next Generation Photovoltaics (NGPV)
og.description: The Center for Next Generation Photovoltaics (NGPV) is addressing the key technological needs to help make solar photovoltaic (PV) electricity a major source of energy in the world.In terms of global electrical energy use, the installed capacity of solar PV allowed it to meet approximately 0.15% (305 gigawatts) of global energy demand as of 2016. By 2030, the total amount of global solar PV capacity could generate enough to meet about 5% of anticipated global energy demand. This presents a significant challenge to the energy sector in relation to solar PV integration, manufacturing, costs, reliability, and access.To reach solar PV deployment of this magnitude, many challenges must be overcome, including:The total cost of PV systems must be reduced, while increasing energy conversion efficiency, reliability, and lifetime.The capacity to cost-effectively manufacture solar cells and balance of systems components must be increased.Methods to integrate solar PV into the utility grid must continue to improve to ensure affordable and reliable electricity.Transportation electrification and advanced building systems must be considered, as they are creating an increase in the application for electricity.Technologies must be improved for energy storage, catalyzed chemicals and fuels production, and water purification.NGPV is helping to establish solar PV electricity as a major source of energy in the United States and the world, by developing new strategies for reducing costs while increasing efficiency. NGPV has targets of $0.05/kilowatt hour (kWh) for residential solar PV and $0.03/kWh for utility-scale solar PV by 2030, to ultimately help significantly reduce carbon emissions.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.evidence: no readable web app manifest; no service worker registered
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
